_setup: 1. Applications > APIs > Create API. Identifier: https://api.example.com
Without an API, Auth0 returns an opaque token and there is no JWT to verify.
2. Applications > Create Application > Single Page Web Applications.
Settings > Allowed Callback URLs: http://localhost:3000/callback. Save.
3. Applications > Create Application > Machine to Machine. Authorise it for the API.
For the user flow, which needs a token without a browser:
4. User Management > Users > Create User, connection Username-Password-Authentication.
5. The SPA > Settings > Advanced Settings > Grant Types: tick Password.
6. Settings > General > API Authorization Settings > Default Directory:
Username-Password-Authentication. Without it the plain password grant is refused,
and the `realm` field below uses Auth0's own variant instead.
The issuer keeps its trailing slash: Auth0 puts one in the `iss` claim.
Auth0 publishes no introspection endpoint, so that check reports `no`.
